title: Aero India 2027 To Be Held In Bengaluru From 8-12 February; Exhibitor Registrations Commences Today
text:
Defence
Swarajya Staff
Sep 03, 2026 | Updated 09:12 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!

The 16th edition of Aero India, Asia's largest air show and one of the world's premier aerospace and defence exhibitions, will take place at Air Force Station Yelahanka in Bengaluru from 8 to 12 February 2027, the Defence Ministry announced on Wednesday (2 September).
Online registration and booking of exhibition space commenced today (3 September) through the official Aero India website.
Organised by the Department of Defence Production, the five-day event will bring together global aerospace and defence companies, policymakers, technology experts, innovators, industry representatives and defence forces personnel.
The biennial exhibition has developed into an important global platform for India's aerospace and defence sector, showcasing the country's expanding manufacturing capabilities, indigenous technologies and emerging innovations.
The event will feature a comprehensive exhibition alongside business and strategic engagements, providing opportunities for industry-to-industry interactions, government-to-industry partnerships, technology demonstrations and collaborations.
Spectacular aerial displays by the Indian Air Force and participating international flying teams will offer visitors an opportunity to witness advanced aviation capabilities in action.
Aero India 2027 is expected to facilitate greater participation from Indian defence industries, including MSMEs and start-ups, while creating avenues for partnerships, investments, exports and technology collaboration.
The previous edition in February 2025 attracted approximately 900 exhibitors, of which 150 were international, along with 26 defence ministers and 118 CEOs from the global aerospace and defence industry.
A dedicated web-based portal has been developed to facilitate seamless participation and provide comprehensive services for exhibitors and visitors.
The ministry said the event would provide significant impetus to India's vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and its emergence as a trusted partner in the global defence and aerospace supply chain.
